newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus archaeologists find 6th Century BC statues.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus archaeologists find 6th Century BC statues.

text.p: Archaeologists in Cyprus on Friday unearthed several immaculately preserved statues of lions and sphinxes which they said dated from the 6th Century BC.

"Our team was working on maintaining the wall of a royal tomb there this morning and they found two lions, over life-sized, and a sphinx in immaculate condition," director of Cyprus Antiquities Department Demos Christou told Reuters.
"They were made around the 6th Century BC. They are archaic, made of limestone," he said of the finds at Tamassos, the site of an ancient kingdom 20 km (12 miles) southwest of the capital Nicosia.
The lions are in a crouching position with their teeth bared. One is missing an ear, while the other was found in three pieces. The sphinx was found intact.
Museum officials said two more statues of lions and another sphinx were found later on Friday.
"If we are lucky we will stumble across something this precious once every 20 years," said one researcher.
Christou said the sphinx was identical to those found in Egyptian museums and noted that Cyprus was under Egyptian rule during the period.

Tamassos, a settlement believed to date from around 1200 BC, was one of 11 to 13 ancient inland kingdoms on Cyprus. The kingdoms were replaced in the 3rd Century BC by the Cypriot Commune, or "Koinon Kyprion", until the 7th Century AD.

"Tamassos was very important because of the copper smelting workshops there and its two ancient tombs entirely made of stone. This find is additional evidence that the site was very very important," Christou said.
